children: For Vicinity Centres, there might be a better alternative to building 480 residential apartments adjacent to its Chatswood Chase mall. That is Morgan Stanley's view after it crunched numbers on what a development could cost. Building 480 units across two buildings could have an end value of A$1.1 billion-A$1.2 billion, analyst Simon Chan says. Development profits from building the apartments could be around A$365 million. But it would require some A$720 million of capex to realize that amount, MS says. "We think the company has a low-risk alternative," MS says. "Just sell the land, which we believe could deliver profit of A$176 million." Monetizing the sites could be good management, given it unlocks capital immediately and avoids further capex, it contends. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
